subject: Clarify commit buckets, throughput entitlements & SLA credit ladder
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aurorify.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorify.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on committed buckets and SLA remedy ladder

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and engineering asked me to follow up with a few concrete asks so we can close the order:

1) We want the contract to define a clear unit for committed capacity. Your SOW calls them “commit units” but doesn’t explicitly map to GPU hours vs vram-hours. Procurement needs a concise definition that we can use for monthly invoicing.

2) Throughput entitlements: our throughput profile is bursty (short spikes to 20k tokens/min). We need to understand how burst capacity is billed vs baseline reserved throughput, and whether you guarantee token-per-second minima for our reserved pool.

3) SLA remedy ladder: we’re proposing a 10/20/30 credit ladder tied to monthly availability bands. Can you confirm Redwood’s position on (a) whether credits are pro-rated by affected route, and (b) whether credits apply when fallback to a lower-tier model occurs (we route to smaller quantized model).

I’ve attached our redlines showing suggested language; procurement would like a written response this week so they can get final sign-off. If it’s easier to discuss, happy to jump on a quick call.

—Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Platform Ops, Aurorify
procurement@aurorify.ai

Attachment: Aurorify_Redlines_20261210.pdf (redlines summary)
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aurorify.ai>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on committed buckets and SLA remedy ladder

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear bullets. Quick answers up front, then a proposed next step:

1) Commit unit definition: we can accept a definition that maps to "vCPU-equivalent GPU-hour" (VEG-hour) for billing simplicity, with a published conversion table per instance type (e.g., A100-80GB = 1.0 VEG/hr, A100-40GB quantized = 0.6 VEG/hr). We will include the conversion table as an appendix. This addresses monthly invoicing alignment.

2) Throughput entitlements and burst: our reserved pool guarantees baseline throughput in tokens/sec per VEG-hour. Burst above baseline is supported via a shared burst band; billing for bursts is charged against reserved bucket first (until exhausted) then billed as on-demand at pre-agreed overage rate. We can add language that guarantees X tokens/sec per VEG at your expected profile and defines burst exhaustion semantics.

3) SLA credits and fallbacks: Redwood’s standard credit ladder is per-tenant monthly availability. We are willing to: (a) tie credits to impacted route(s) when a customer defines dedicated routes in config, and (b) exclude fallbacks that are intentionally configured as "accepted degradations" by the customer. For unplanned automatic fallback to lower-tier models due to capacity constraints, credits should apply if the fallback causes a measurable SLO breach.

Next step: Sean and I drafted proposed contract language and a compact credit ladder that attempts to meet you halfway. Can we schedule 30 minutes Mon morning PST to walk through our phrasing and your redlines? I’ve attached our draft language and a sample commit amortization sheet.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Director, Sales — Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Commit_Language_20261211.docx, Commit_Amortization_Sample.xlsx
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aurorify.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorify.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on committed buckets and SLA remedy ladder

Vanessa/Sean —

Thanks for the quick reply and for proposing the VEG-hour abstraction. Procurement pushed back on a couple of points after internal review: they want a) stronger limits on overage rates (cap per month), and b) a clearer remedy band for partial outages that impact only our inference-heavy route (i.e., our chat route). They also requested that credits not be conditioned on customers marking fallbacks as "accepted degradations" post-hoc.

I’ve attached an updated redline (Aurorify_Redlines_20261214.pdf) that:
- Proposes a monthly overage cap equal to 25% of the committed spend (so bursts cannot create runaway bills)
- Proposes a 3-band remedy ladder specific to route-level availability:
  * >= 99.9%: no credit
  * 99.0%–99.9%: 10% credit on that route’s monthly fees
  * <99.0%: 25% credit on that route’s monthly fees

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a per-route ladder (instead of tenant-wide) and whether you can agree to the overage cap number?

If helpful, we can trade on committed term length — procurement has room to extend to a 36-month committed bucket for a deeper discount if the remedies are clarified. Happy to take this on our call today at 11am PST; otherwise email responses are fine.

—Jordan

Attachment: Aurorify_Redlines_20261214.pdf
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aurorify.ai>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on committed buckets and SLA remedy ladder

Jordan —

Thanks — great context. Follow-up after our 11am sync (notes below) and a suggested redline to move us toward signature. High-level positions confirmed in the call:

- Commit unit: Redwood will accept the VEG-hour as the canonical billing unit and will ship the instance-type conversion appendix with the SOW.

- Overage cap: Redwood can accept a monthly overage cap of 25% of committed spend for a 36-month committed term (AUR-36M), in exchange for a 15% downward adjustment to the standard per-VEG price. For shorter terms (12/24 mo) we can negotiate a lower cap or a higher per-unit premium.

- Route-level remedy ladder: Redwood will accept a route-specific credit ladder if Aurorify provides a clear list of dedicated routes in the configuration repo. We will adopt your 3-band ladder with two changes: 1) credits will be calculated against the route's allocated monthly committed spend (not total tenant spend), and 2) for automatic fallbacks triggered by capacity constraints, credits will apply if the measured latency or availability delta versus baseline exceeds the SLO threshold for that route.

- Documentation & language: See attached proposed redline (Redwood_Suggested_Redline_20261215.pdf) with concrete wording for VEG-hour, burst band exhaustion, overage cap, and the remedy ladder formula. Key excerpt: "Service Credit = (RouteCommittedSpend) * CreditBand% * (OutageWindowMinutes / MinutesInMonth)". This keeps credits proportional and auditable.

- Next steps:
  1) I’ll share the suggested redline in DocuSign-friendly format by EOD tomorrow.
  2) Karthik will add the conversion table to the SOW appendix.
  3) Sean will scope an engineering runbook for route tagging and metrics we need to support per-route crediting.

If Aurorify agrees, we can finalize signature-ready language and lock the 36-month pricing by COB next Friday.

Appreciate the flexibility — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Director, Sales — Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Suggested_Redline_20261215.pdf
